A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, task, core method, and experiments. Their complete main texts and appendices, including rotated tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original citation-classification experiments, evaluations of 945 summaries for 105 papers, and a study involving nine professors and 82 papers.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds dataset validation, long-tail coverage analysis, error case studies, and Qwen/Gemini experiments.

M1.justification: The intent-generation, citation-filtering, and time-aware summarization pipeline remains unchanged, as do the prompts and output schema in Appendices B–D. The expanded fine-grained-intent definition clarifies the existing representation; Qwen and Gemini are additional implementations tested with the same approach.

E1.justification: The citation datasets, three disciplinary domains, paper-summary tasks, and practical applications remain the same. New analyses examine retained coverage. The revised 1,000 PST-Bench plus 1,000 pattern-matched positive-example description already appeared in v1 Appendix F.1, so it does not establish a dataset replacement.

E2.justification: Structural Scaffolds, Meaningful Citations, Multi-cite, and the trivial classification baselines remain unchanged in the corresponding comparison. The five summarization input variants are also retained. Qwen/Gemini experiments instantiate those variants with different models rather than introduce distinct comparison methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds a computer-science-only confirmatory/correction comparison, a 100-example label audit, and long-tail coverage evaluation using 10 selected themes across 10 papers and 50 summaries. Appendix G.8 also introduces Qwen-2.5-72B and Gemini-2.5-flash experimental configurations. These substantially extend the evaluation design.

E4.justification: New analyses test label quality, performance differences between confirmatory and correction citations, coverage of infrequent meaningful themes, and generalization across model families. Appendix G.7 adds downstream error cases involving false impact classifications and removal of relevant citation evidence. Existing shot-count and disciplinary analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 Table 6 reports annotator F1 agreement of 0.86/0.77/0.85; v2 Table 8 instead reports Cohen’s kappa of 0.68/0.20/0.34. v2 also removes the human–LLM F1 agreement row while retaining Spearman/Kendall correlations and significance reporting. The stated five-run shot experiment and three-run classification voting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The original headline classification and GPT-4o ablation scores are retained. Added results include 90% correctness in the label audit, confirmatory/correction F1 of 0.88/0.98 for the proposed classifier, and long-tail coverage reaching 0.50 for all citations with intents versus 0.40 for impact-revealing citations with intents. Table 13 adds model-specific results, including Gemini faithfulness of 0.96 and citation-year compliance of 0.93.

T1.justification: Neither version develops mathematical theory or proofs. The expanded definition of fine-grained intent explains the existing free-form representation, and long-tail coverage applies coverage measurement to a selected subset without introducing substantive mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain time-aware impact summarization from fine-grained confirmation/correction intents, a reference-free evaluation framework, and demonstrated expert usefulness. The human–LLM alignment claim remains in the abstract and introduction despite its removal from the conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking classifier advantages to correction citations and summary errors to upstream intent mistakes. It discusses model-dependent tradeoffs, broader forms of scientific impact, and bibliographic-data completeness. These qualify and extend the existing interpretation without replacing the central account.

D1.justification: New Appendix H specifies task-to-model assignments, model snapshots, temperatures, and token capacities. v2 also documents confidence-based annotation adjudication and data-quality safeguards, and updates the project link. Conversely, v1’s disclosure of 50 human–LLM evaluation instances per metric is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gemini 2.5 and Qwen3 technical-report citations and explicitly distinguishes its impact/temporal task from RAG approaches. The scientific-impact positioning table is retained. Most other reference changes update bibliographic metadata rather than introduce different works.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies definitions, condenses several passages, and renames the citation-free summarization baseline from zero-shot to no-knowledge. Shot-count details move to Appendix F, while existing human-study feedback and participant information move into the main text. The overall narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds tables for the new analyses, model examples, and configurations, plus a main-text excerpt of existing training examples. The usefulness chart moves into the main text and the shot-count plot moves to the appendix. Figure 10 drops the accuracy bars; most existing display designs are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation through Qwen/Gemini experiments, a label audit, and targeted coverage/error analyses, while resolving the dataset-description inconsistency and adding reproducibility details. The gains are limited by small targeted samples and continued reliance on GPT-4o judging. Reporting also remains uneven: the limitations still claim only GPT-4o was tested, and the human–LLM evaluation sample count disappears. Overall, the additions provide a useful but bounded quality improvement.
